transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-20
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM), Samir Khan (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Aurora Head of ML), Derek Wu (Aurora Eng Manager), Priya Nair (Aurora SRE)

Summary:
Quarterly business review / health check focused on usage trends, cost spikes in December, recent reliability incident on 2026-01-08, and roadmap discussion for Dedicated capacity pilot. Customer is evaluating Dedicated vs private deployment for regulatory reasons. Agreed to run performance benchmarks and share security/compliance docs.

Topics: usage and cost, reliability / incidents, request routing and fallback, Dedicated capacity pricing, security/compliance, next steps / pilot timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off - this is the QBR / health check for Aurora. Maya, Samir with me. Lena, Derek, Priya from Aurora - want to do quick intros?
[00:10] Lena Ortiz: Hi, Lena Ortiz, Head of ML. We've been using Redwood for chat and embeddings in Prod.
[00:14] Derek Wu: Derek, Eng manager, focusing on infra and cost.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Priya, SRE, I can talk about incidents and monitoring.
[00:22] Jordan Lee: Great. I'll run through high-level usage and cost, then Samir will cover performance notes and Maya will go through support and security asks.
[00:29] Jordan Lee: Quick numbers - on the hosted API you've been averaging about 9.2M tokens per week in Q4, steady growth month over month. Noticed a cost bump mid-December — is that when you shifted more traffic to the high-reply model?
[00:45] Derek Wu: Yeah that 12/14 deploy had longer responses. We saw p50 latency increase but cost per session jumped 28%. We're trying to correlate with prompt changes.
[00:55] Lena Ortiz: Also we ran a batch of reranking jobs over the holidays which ate tokens, some were mis-scheduled.
[01:04] Jordan Lee: Makes sense. On our side we can tweak batching and prefix caching to reduce tokens for reranking - Samir, do you want to cover cache impact?
[01:11] Samir Khan: Sure. So the KV-cache and prefix caching can cut repeated token generation by ~40% for your pattern; continuous batching could also reduce unit cost but latency tradeoffs. On your average session we estimate 20-30% cost reduction with conservative settings. But need to run your real prompts to be precise.
[01:28] Derek Wu: That would help. Our main concern is p99 latency — we need <300ms for interactive agents. In December we had spikes to 1.2s p99 around 12/14 incident.
[01:39] Priya Nair: Right, we saw error rates climb during a capacity contention window, fallback to smaller model wasn't clean, there was some mis-routing back to hosted that caused auth hiccups.
[01:50] Maya Patel: Thanks for flagging that — we logged that incident (INC-2026-011). Samir, quick note on fallbacks?
[01:56] Samir Khan: Our smart routing should've auto-failed to the warm pool; sounds like the routing policy for Aurora was set to prefer hosted over dedicated variants, so fallback path had an auth mismatch. We pushed a fix last week to standardize the token validation in fallback.
[02:12] Lena Ortiz: Ok good. For compliance, leadership wants either Dedicated or Private (VPC) — data residency and KMS integration are blockers for private customers. Maya, can you remind us of the Private offering timeline?
[02:24] Maya Patel: Sure. Private VPC is generally available now for larger contracts; on-prem package is GA in Q2. For Aurora size we recommend starting with a Dedicated pilot (reserved capacity) to get predictable latency and isolation, then evaluate Private if you need on-prem.
[02:36] Derek Wu: Cost question — what's delta between hosted high-tier and Dedicated reserved?
[02:40] Jordan Lee: Dedicated is a committed monthly price that significantly reduces per-token unit costs at scale — we provided a ballpark in the deck: for your 9M tokens/week profile, Dedicated committed 2-3x capacity reduces unit cost by ~35-45% depending on GPU mix and quantization. We'll send updated numbers tailored to your profile.
[02:58] Derek Wu: Great. Also want to validate SLA and SLOs — p99 targets and credits.
[03:03] Maya Patel: We can provide SLA language in the enterprise addendum. For Dedicated we can commit to a p99 latency target per model family and an uptime SLA. We'll share typical SLOs from similar customers.
[03:15] Priya Nair: For security, we need SOC2, ISO, KMS integration details, and audit log retention options for at least 2 years.
[03:23] Maya Patel: We'll email SOC2 and ISO artifacts; KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated with customer-managed keys — and we have audit logs in the console. I'll send retention options.
[03:32] Lena Ortiz: On the model roadmap, are there plans to onboard Llama/Redwood-verified newer open models or Mistral variants? We want to compare quality vs cost.
[03:41] Samir Khan: We're validating a few quantized Mistral variants and a 30B Llama-derived family. Redwood maintains a model catalog with verified performance profiles; we can run evals with your prompt set to recommend quantization and model family. That will show tradeoffs between latency, cost, and hallucination rate.
[03:57] Derek Wu: Let's do evals. We'll give 3 canonical prompts and expected outputs.
[04:02] Jordan Lee: Perfect. For the pilot timeline — proposal: run a 4-week Dedicated pilot with reserved capacity and benchmarking in week 1, run KV-cache and batching tests week 2-3, then review results week 4 and decide on commit. Does that align?
[04:17] Lena Ortiz: Sounds reasonable. We need to align with procurement too — contract review may take 2-3 weeks.
[04:22] Maya Patel: We'll put a pilot proposal together and include pricing and SLOs.
[04:26] Priya Nair: One more point — log ingestion for monitoring: can we send our Prometheus metrics to the Redwood console or does Redwood provide a forwarder?
[04:35] Samir Khan: We provide tracing hooks and can accept push metrics to our observability endpoint; alternatively, we can configure remote write. I'll follow up with the spec.
[04:44] Derek Wu: On benchmarking: can you run a 64 concurrent session test with our real prompts and show p50/p95/p99 plus token cost per request?
[04:52] Samir Khan: Yes — need the prompt set and an API key for a test project. We'll spin up a dedicated bench runner and share a spreadsheet.
[05:00] Jordan Lee: Recap / Actions: Jordan to send tailored Dedicated pricing and SLOs; Samir to run KV-cache + batching perf and a 64-concurrency bench; Maya to send SOC2/ISO and RBAC/SSO checklist; Derek to share 3 prompts and p95/p99 logs. We'll target next sync after benchmarks.
[05:18] Lena Ortiz: Thanks, team. A couple caveats: procurement needs a clear data residency statement and the ability to rotate keys monthly.
[05:26] Maya Patel: Noted — we'll include KMS rotation options in the docs.
[05:29] Jordan Lee: Any competitors you're evaluating?
[05:31] Derek Wu: We looked at Anthropic for safety but OpenAI for feature parity; Vertex AI for integration with GCP. But Redwood's dedicated offering and cost projections are compelling.
[05:41] Priya Nair: Also want to see long-term retention pricing — embeddings storage costs have been creeping up.
[05:47] Jordan Lee: We'll include embeddings cost optimization notes — caching, dimensionality reduction, and deduping.
[05:52] Samir Khan: One more: we'll add a recommended quantization profile that balances latency and accuracy for your domain.
[05:59] Jordan Lee: Great. We'll wrap — thanks everyone, we'll send the deck and the action items in an email.
[06:06] Lena Ortiz: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes on transcription quality: Some noise around system names (we occasionally transcribed 'KV' as 'kay vee'), and a couple spots of crosstalk. The timestamps are approximate.
